issues.claim: https://www.ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-335/ cited for "По модели обработки исключений CLI (ECMA-335) исключение, возникшее внутри фильтра, ... отбрасывается, а фильтр считается вернувшим false"
issues.problem: The fetched excerpt is only the ECMA landing page (a list of partitions and download links). It does not show the swallow-and-treat-as-false rule. The generator itself did not verify the clause. I recall this rule is in Partition I (exception handling overview), but nothing in the item confirms it.
issues.suggestedFix: Cite the specific clause (ECMA-335 Partition I, 12.4.2 exception handling, filter blocks), or link a page that shows the text. A good alternative is the CoreCLR BOTR exceptions doc or the C# spec section on the try statement. If the text cannot be shown, soften the explanation so it does not attribute the rule to a specific ECMA clause.

issues.claim: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/language-reference/keywords/when cited as a source for the filter behaviour
issues.problem: The excerpt covers only the syntax of `when` and the benefits of exception filters. It never mentions an exception thrown inside a filter being swallowed. The page supports the general `when` explanation but not the core claim.
issues.suggestedFix: Keep the link as a general reference for `when`. Add a source that states the swallow-and-false semantics (the C# spec try statement section or the BOTR exceptions doc), and update linkTitles in both locales.

issues.claim: Can an exception raised while the `when` condition is being checked replace the exception for which a handler is being searched?
issues.problem: The hint almost states the key idea (the original exception is kept), so it nudges strongly toward the answer. The Russian hint matches it.
issues.suggestedFix: Make it more neutral, for example: "What does the runtime do with an exception that escapes from a filter expression while it is looking for a handler?" Apply the same change to the ru hint.

issues.claim: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/language-reference/statements/iteration-statements cited for "Компилятор разворачивает foreach ... и в этом finally вызывает Dispose перечислителя"
issues.problem: The excerpt shows the for and foreach basics but not the Dispose-in-finally expansion of foreach. I cannot confirm from the excerpt that this page supports the claim. The `Dispose` claim is correct, and the sandbox result and the classes spec excerpt confirm the iterator side.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace this link, or add one, pointing to the C# language specification statements page, foreach section. That section describes the try/finally with Dispose expansion. Update linkTitles in ru and en.

issues.claim: `foreach` and the LINQ operators do it for you
issues.problem: This is broader than the sources show. Most LINQ operators dispose source enumerators, but the sources do not state it and operators that stop early are the relevant case.
issues.suggestedFix: Say "`foreach` and the LINQ operators that enumerate a source (for example `First`, `Take`) dispose the enumerator", or drop the LINQ mention. Apply the same change to the ru text.
